claims.text: A DFT-based computational method can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The DFT-based method will improve predictive accuracy by at least 15% relative to empirical or simplified computational approaches.
The target materials are high-entropy alloys in their as-cast state.
Ab initio DFT calculations will be used to predict phonon dispersion and thermal conductivity.
The proposed operating range is 300 K to 1000 K at ambient pressure.
Phonon-scattering rates and lattice distortion mediate the thermal-conductivity behavior.
The DFT-based approach accurately captures interactions among the different elements in high-entropy alloys.
Capturing interelement interactions improves predictions of phonon-scattering rates and thermal conductivity.
The method will predict thermal-conductivity values at least 10% lower than current approaches predict.
A 10% reduction in predicted thermal conductivity corresponds to a 15% improvement in predictive accuracy.
The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing no more than five principal elements.
The method may not be suitable for alloys containing complex precipitate phases or high porosity.
Experimental thermal conductivity can be measured by laser flash and compared with DFT-based predictions.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted thermal-conductivity values differ from experimental values by more than 20%.
